source.title: Optimize TSK Fuzzy Systems for Big Data Classification Problems: Bag of Tricks

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no material truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own MBGD-based TSK classifier results, including training loss comparisons with and without batch normalization. The model and tasks differ from the versions’ neural network settings, but this directly tests the related claim that normalization affects gradient-training convergence.
record.gate_note: The paper reports classification accuracy, rule firing levels, training loss and gradient norms for TSK fuzzy classifiers. Those results do not measure the training classification error, local minima, depth, initialization effects, learning-rate stability, or BN speed claims in the listed versions, except the BN training-loss comparison relevant to V6. References to earlier BN work are cited background, not results of this paper.
record.test_reason: The study extends BN to TSK fuzzy classifiers and evaluates its own training method. Its results concern fuzzy rule systems, rather than the neural networks named in V6. Lower training loss and larger gradients in these systems do not establish V6's accuracy-speed or higher-learning-rate claims. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: UR and consequent-input BN each help TSK fuzzy classification, and combining them gives the strongest overall performance. The authors also claim faster convergence with BN. The combined method has the best average BCA rank and second-best average RCA rank, rather than winning every dataset or metric.
record.recipe_differences: Mini-batch AdaBound optimization of TSK fuzzy classifiers; BN is applied to rule consequents, not the neural network recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: On the Satellite dataset, the BN variant affected training loss and test BCA; among BN variants, the standard BN approach had the best average BCA and global BN the worst. Batch size also affected test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: On Satellite, BN variants had lower early training loss and better test BCA; curves summarize 10 runs over the first 20 epochs, with UR weight fixed to 1 where applicable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN applied to TSK rule consequents can improve early optimization and test performance in fuzzy classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: On Satellite, BN increased the L1 norms of antecedent and consequent parameter gradients during early training. Gradient magnitude alone does not measure accuracy gain speed or learning-rate tolerance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN can increase parameter-gradient magnitudes in TSK fuzzy classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 12 datasets, consequent-only BN had average test BCA 0.7404, versus 0.7121 without BN, 0.7106 with global BN and 0.7265 with rule-specific BN; all these comparisons included UR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The placement of BN affects generalization performance in TSK fuzzy classifiers.

record.problems: The BN training-loss, test-BCA and gradient-norm comparisons are figure-only in the supplied text, without exact values or stated uncertainty for those curves. Experiments are on TSK fuzzy classifiers and do not establish the specified deep neural network claims.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows for the listed versions: the paper's reported results do not measure those versions' target behaviors. BN convergence evidence is described textually but its quantitative figure values are unavailable in the supplied text, and it does not measure V6's specified model settings or training-accuracy speed measure.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including random labels and the effects of capacity, stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, and initialization-based alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, orthogonality, training speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence.
BN's effects on neural-network accuracy gain speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free residual training.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification and V6 tested status should be corrected. There are no extracted rows to fix. The out-of-version BN findings are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error; corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping and regularization on that error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects, identity shortcuts, special initialization of plain networks, and normalization-free residual networks.
Activation-matched initializations, signal or gradient propagation across depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep convolutional networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, loss recovery, sharpness dynamics and divergence.

Tests BN's training-loss effect in TSK fuzzy classifiers, not the specified sigmoid/MNIST, VGG/CIFAR-10 or Inception/ImageNet settings, nor accuracy gain speed or higher learning-rate tolerance. It does not test Fixup.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
